target: Il est possible que nous déménagions l'année prochaine.
english: It's possible we'll move next year.
tip: "Il est possible que" expresses uncertainty and triggers the subjunctive.

target: Si j'avais su, je ne serais pas venu.
english: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.
tip: Si + plus-que-parfait → conditionnel passé: this expresses an unreal past condition.

target: Si j'avais une voiture, je n'aurais pas besoin du bus.
english: If I had a car, I wouldn't need the bus.
tip: 'Tu aurais pu me le dire !' = You could have told me! Conditionnel passé for reproach or missed opportunities.

target: Bien qu'il pleuve, nous allons sortir.
english: Although it's raining, we're going out.
tip: "Bien que" (although) always requires the subjunctive.

target: Je suis déçu que le concert soit annulé.
english: I'm disappointed the concert is cancelled.
tip: Adjectives of emotion + que trigger the subjunctive: soit, not est.

target: Il est naturel que vous ayez des questions.
english: It's natural that you have questions.
tip: Subjunctive after 'le seul/la seule qui': 'c'est le seul qui sache' – uniqueness triggers subjunctive.

target: Tu devrais lire ce livre, il est passionnant.
english: You should read this book, it's fascinating.
tip: Conditional `-rais/-rait/-rions/-riez/-raient` = 'would'. `J'aimerais` = 'I would like' (polite). `Je voudrais un café` is way more polite than `je veux un café`.

target: Il est dommage que nous ne puissions pas rester.
english: It's a shame we can't stay.
tip: "Puissions" is the subjunctive of pouvoir. "Il est dommage que" expresses regret.

target: C'est la plus belle ville que j'aie jamais visitée.
english: It's the most beautiful city I've ever visited.
tip: Superlatives trigger the subjunctive in relative clauses.

target: Je te prête mon vélo pourvu que tu fasses attention.
english: I'll lend you my bike provided you're careful.
tip: "Pourvu que" (provided that) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Avant que tu ne t'en ailles, j'ai quelque chose à te dire.
english: Before you leave, I have something to tell you.
tip: In formal French, an expletive "ne" can appear after "avant que" without negative meaning.

target: Elle exige que les employés soient ponctuels.
english: She demands that the employees be punctual.
tip: "Exiger que" (to demand that) triggers the subjunctive.

target: Explique-lui la situation calmement.
english: Explain the situation to him calmly.
tip: In positive imperatives with two pronouns, the indirect object comes second: Explique-lui.

target: Réfléchis bien avant de répondre.
english: Think carefully before answering.
tip: The tu-form of '-ir' verbs keeps the final '-s' in imperatives: 'Finis tes devoirs !' (Finish your homework!). Only '-er' verbs drop it.

target: Asseyez-vous et attendez votre tour.
english: Sit down and wait for your turn.
tip: 'Asseyez-vous' – reflexive imperative: the pronoun goes after with a hyphen. Negative: 'ne vous asseyez pas'.

target: Fais tes devoirs avant de jouer.
english: Do your homework before playing.
tip: "Fais" is the tu-form imperative of faire. Irregular: fais, faisons, faites.

target: Voyons ce que nous pouvons faire.
english: Let's see what we can do.
tip: 'Vas-y' – imperative of aller + y. The -s reappears before 'y' for pronunciation: vas-y, not *va-y.

target: Je paierai l'addition, c'est mon tour.
english: I'll pay the bill, it's my turn.
tip: Futur simple of payer: paierai. The -y- changes to -i- before mute -e-.

target: Tu pourrais me rendre un service ?
english: Could you do me a favor?
tip: 'Pouvoir' in conditional: 'tu pourrais' (you could). Very common for polite requests.

target: Je t'appellerai dès que j'arrive à l'aéroport.
english: I'll call you as soon as I arrive at the airport.
tip: 'Dès que' + future (not present like in English): 'dès que j'arriverai'. French uses future after time conjunctions.

target: Tu ne devrais pas manger autant de sucre.
english: You shouldn't eat so much sugar.
tip: Negative conditional: ne + conditional + pas. Tu ne devrais pas = you shouldn't.

target: Écris ton nom en haut de la page.
english: Write your name at the top of the page.
tip: 'Écris' – tu-form imperative of écrire (irregular). Regular -ir/-re verbs keep the -s in imperative.

target: Ils vont repeindre leur appartement pendant les vacances.
english: They're going to repaint their apartment during the vacation.
tip: `aller + infinitive` = the everyday future, like English 'going to': `je vais manger` = 'I'm going to eat'. Way more common in speech than the textbook future tense (`je mangerai`).

target: Si vous veniez samedi, nous pourrions dîner ensemble.
english: If you came on Saturday, we could have dinner together.
tip: 'On pourrait aller au restaurant' = We could go to the restaurant. Conditionnel of pouvoir for gentle suggestions.

target: Si tu lui parlais, je suis sûr qu'il comprendrait.
english: If you talked to him, I'm sure he would understand.
tip: 'Il comprendrait si tu lui expliquais' – note: si + imparfait, main clause + conditionnel. The tense pairing is fixed.

target: On va commander une pizza, ça te va ?
english: We're going to order a pizza, is that okay with you?
tip: Three parts: form of `aller`, then directly the infinitive. No `à` or `de` between them.

target: Je vais préparer le dîner pendant que tu te reposes.
english: I'm going to make dinner while you rest.
tip: 'Je vais préparer' – futur proche: aller (present) + infinitive. Natural in everyday speech.

target: Sois patient, ton tour va arriver.
english: Be patient, your turn will come.
tip: "Sois" is the irregular tu-form imperative of être: sois, soyons, soyez.

target: Ne vous inquiétez pas, tout ira bien.
english: Don't worry, everything will be fine.
tip: Negative reflexive imperative: Ne + pronoun + verb + pas. Ne vous inquiétez pas.

target: Elle aimerait vivre à Paris un jour.
english: She would like to live in Paris someday.
tip: The conditional makes requests polite: 'Je voudrais' (I would like) instead of 'Je veux' (I want). Essential for ordering in cafés and shops.

target: On va bientôt savoir si le projet est accepté.
english: We'll soon know if the project is accepted.
tip: 'Quand' + futur simple (not present): 'quand il arrivera' = when he arrives. French marks futurity explicitly.

target: Je serais ravi de vous aider avec votre projet.
english: I would be delighted to help you with your project.
tip: 'Devoir' in conditional: 'tu devrais' = you should. Very common for giving advice.

target: Si nous habitions à la campagne, nous aurions un grand jardin.
english: If we lived in the countryside, we would have a big garden.
tip: 'J'aurais dû' = I should have. 'Aurais' + past participle expresses regret about the past. Very common in spoken French.

target: Nous allons partir dans cinq minutes.
english: We're going to leave in five minutes.
tip: Futur proche: aller (present) + infinitive. Used for near future or certain events.

target: L'avion décollera à quinze heures trente.
english: The plane will take off at three thirty.
tip: 'Décollera' – futur simple for scheduled events (flights, trains). Common in announcements.

target: Tu finiras par comprendre, ne t'inquiète pas.
english: You'll end up understanding, don't worry.
tip: "Finir par" + infinitive = to end up doing something. Finiras = futur simple of finir.

target: La personne dont tu as besoin viendra demain.
english: The person you need will come tomorrow.
tip: Avoir besoin de → dont: "la personne dont tu as besoin."

target: Voici le restaurant qui fait les meilleures pizzas.
english: Here's the restaurant that makes the best pizzas.
tip: "Qui" is used for subjects: le restaurant fait → le restaurant qui fait.

target: Il faudrait que tu prennes rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
english: You should make an appointment at the dentist.
tip: 'Il faudrait que' + subjunctive – conditional of 'falloir' for polite necessity: 'you should...'

target: Ça me plairait de vivre dans un pays chaud.
english: I would enjoy living in a warm country.
tip: After 'quand même' (anyway), conditional is common: 'je le ferais quand même' = I'd do it anyway.

target: Je vais te prêter mon livre quand je l'aurai fini.
english: I'm going to lend you my book when I've finished it.
tip: Futur proche emphasizes intention: 'je vais le faire' (I'm going to do it). Futur simple: 'je le ferai' (I'll do it).

target: Le livre que j'ai lu est passionnant.
english: The book I read is fascinating.
tip: "Que" replaces the direct object. In passé composé, the past participle agrees with "que" (masculine singular here).

target: Bien qu'il eût raison, personne ne le croyait.
english: Although he was right, no one believed him.
tip: Imperfect subjunctive of avoir: eût. Literary equivalent of 'bien qu'il ait raison'.

target: Elles iront en vacances en Espagne cet été.
english: They will go on vacation to Spain this summer.
tip: Use futur simple for promises and predictions: 'J'irai, c'est promis' (I'll go, I promise). Futur proche for what's about to happen.

target: Dès qu'il fera beau, nous irons à la plage.
english: As soon as the weather is nice, we'll go to the beach.
tip: After "dès que" and "quand," French uses the futur simple, unlike English.

target: Si j'avais le permis, je conduirais pour aller au travail.
english: If I had my license, I would drive to work.
tip: 'Je conduirais si je n'avais pas bu' = I would drive if I hadn't drunk. Conditional for unreal present situations.

target: Ils travailleront ensemble l'année prochaine.
english: They will work together next year.
tip: French has two futures: futur simple ('je travaillerai' – more formal/distant) and futur proche ('je vais travailler' – imminent/certain).

target: Lorsque tu seras rentré, préviens-moi.
english: When you've gotten home, let me know.
tip: Futur antérieur with être: seras rentré. Rentrer uses être.

target: Nous allons déménager le mois prochain.
english: We're going to move next month.
tip: Futur proche is preferred for planned or imminent events: nous allons déménager.

target: J'avais déjà vu ce film trois fois.
english: I had already seen this movie three times.
tip: In plus-que-parfait, adverbs like "déjà" go between the auxiliary and participle: avais déjà vu.

target: Les étudiants qui ont réussi l'examen sont contents.
english: The students who passed the exam are happy.
tip: 'Qui' replaces the subject: 'les étudiants qui ont réussi' – 'qui' is the subject of 'ont réussi'.

target: Voici le collègue dont je t'ai souvent parlé.
english: Here is the colleague I've often told you about.
tip: 'Dont' replaces 'de + qui/quoi': 'le collègue dont je t'ai parlé' = whom I told you about (parler de).

target: Le cadeau que j'ai reçu m'a fait très plaisir.
english: The gift I received made me very happy.
tip: With "que" + passé composé, the past participle agrees with the antecedent: reçu (masculine singular).

target: Elle avait appris la nouvelle par un ami commun.
english: She had learned the news through a mutual friend.
tip: Plus-que-parfait of apprendre: avait appris. Irregular past participle: appris.

target: Tu verras, tout ira bien.
english: You'll see, everything will be fine.
tip: 'On verra' = We'll see. One of the most common French expressions, used to defer a decision.

target: Nous ne pourrons pas venir samedi.
english: We won't be able to come on Saturday.
tip: Futur simple of pouvoir: pourrai, pourras, pourra, pourrons, pourrez, pourront.

target: Nous vous enverrons les documents par courriel.
english: We will send you the documents by email.
tip: 'Envoyer' has an irregular future stem: 'enverr-'. 'Je t'enverrai un message' = I'll send you a message.

target: Le repas que nous avons partagé était mémorable.
english: The meal we shared was memorable.
tip: 'Lequel/laquelle' after prepositions: 'la raison pour laquelle' = the reason for which.

target: Si tu étudies bien, tu réussiras ton examen.
english: If you study well, you'll pass your exam.
tip: Si + présent → futur simple. Note: never use futur after "si" (if).

target: Je ferai de mon mieux pour terminer à temps.
english: I'll do my best to finish on time.
tip: 'Qu'est-ce qu'on fera ?' = What will we do? 'Faire' in future tense is essential for making plans.
